rationale: The book's core identification of righteousness as the doing of God's commandments (right-living under the law, embodied as righteous acts) is directly established by the three printed texts and is carried consistently through the garment imagery and related passages. The strongest counter (forensic/imputed status as primary, with acts secondary or optional) is answered by the book's careful handling of the reckoning texts (Romans 4; Philippians 3:9), the filthy-rags text, and the 'given then worn' grammar of Revelation 19:8/Ephesians 2:10; those texts do not require redefining righteousness as a verdict without deeds. Prior accepted findings on belief, faith, and love (all requiring obedient response) reinforce rather than contradict the identification. No material detail in the supplied evidence is left unexplained or better explained by the counter.
book_core_identification: Righteousness is the doing of God's commandments—the law kept as right-living, worn as the garment of righteous acts—not a vague goodness nor a verdict only received.
book_secondary_elaborations: Righteous acts are granted by God (ordained, given linen) then put on by the wearer, not self-manufactured as wage-debt
Garment can be soiled by the wearer's uncleanness and must be washed (blood of the Lamb, foot-washing of walk) rather than discarded
Nakedness is covenant exposure/shame; fig-leaf coverings are self-cut and fruitless
God's own righteousness is His right-living/ways by definition; armor pieces are His war-dress lent as clothing
Covenant grammar unites name owned and garment worn
strongest_counter_interpretation: Righteousness primarily denotes forensic right standing before God—Christ's righteousness imputed/credited to the believer through faith alone, independent of works of law—functioning as a legal status (justification) that may later produce ethical fruit but is itself a received verdict, not the doing of commandments.
counter_core_identification: Forensic/imputed status of right standing received by faith, apart from works
material_core_denial: The counter denies that the doing of the commandments is the substance of righteousness itself, treating such doing as either excluded from the definition (as 'works') or as merely secondary fruit of a prior non-deed status.
counter_case: Genesis 15:6 / Romans 4:3-8 reckon faith as righteousness apart from works, with David’s non-imputation of sin as the model
Romans 3:21-26 and Philippians 3:9 contrast righteousness of God through faith with righteousness of one’s own from law
2 Corinthians 5:21 and Isaiah 61:10 present righteousness as a gift/robe bestowed rather than performed
Protestant consensus and Reformation readings take the dominant sense as forensic declaration covering the sinner
book_explanatory_advantages: Direct lexical match to Deut 6:25, Ps 119:172, 1 John 3:7 without redefinition
Rev 19:8 dikaiōmata (righteous acts/deeds) is plural and active; KJV narrowing to 'righteousness' is corrected by the chapter’s grammar of given-then-worn
Reckoning texts are read as excluding wage-debt claims and covering sin, not as emptying righteousness of right-living; Abraham’s prior obedience and James 2:22 fit without tension
Isa 64:6 is the uncleanness of the doer staining the acts, not the acts themselves being filth; washing texts restore rather than replace the garment
Consistent with prior full findings on belief/faith/love as requiring commandment-keeping response
counter_explanatory_advantages: Accounts for the strong Pauline emphasis on grace and the exclusion of boasting/works as debt
Matches the dominant historical Protestant reading of justification
decisive_sources: Romans 4:4-8 (grace vs debt; forgiveness of wrong-living)
Philippians 3:9,12,16 (source contrast + walk by the same rule)
Isaiah 61:10 + Ephesians 2:10 (garments given then walked in)
unresolved_objections: Some Pauline 'righteousness of God' texts remain polyvalent and can still be read primarily as divine faithfulness or forensic gift even after the book’s source-vs-substance distinction
The exact relation of pre-conversion works versus post-grace ordained deeds is not exhaustively quantified in every verse
